title: Agents vs Workflows: Why Not Both? — Sam Bhagwat, Mastra.ai
talk_summary: Sam Bhagwat argues the agents-vs-workflows debate is a false choice: agents are turn-based/open-ended, workflows are dependency/control structures, and production systems should compose them. He recommends readable workflow code, splitting unreliable LLM calls, scoping tools, and using supervisor/handoff patterns with tracing because non-determinism makes observability critical.

takeaways.technique: Compose agents and workflows as interchangeable primitives
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat an agent as a workflow step and a workflow as an agent tool, so deterministic control flow can wrap open-ended agent calls where needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an agent can be a step a workflow can be a tool an agent can be a tool a workflow can be a step

takeaways.technique: Split one unreliable LLM call into structured subcalls
takeaways.what_they_do: When a single large prompt is inaccurate, decompose it into multiple narrower LLM calls with explicit structure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Have you considered breaking that one LM call into 12 LM calls?

takeaways.technique: Dynamic tool injection / scope tools per task
takeaways.what_they_do: Limit which tools an agent sees for a given task instead of exposing all tools all the time, because too many tools degrade agent performance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents um can start failing if you give them let's say double-digit numbers of tools

takeaways.technique: Supervisor agent calls specialized agents as tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Use an orchestrator agent that invokes narrower research/summary/review agents as tools and combines their outputs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent supervisor model you have an agent that is calling other agents as tools

takeaways.technique: Step-level tracing and replay for non-deterministic workflows
takeaways.what_they_do: Because AI workflows are non-deterministic, make execution traceable and replayable at workflow-step boundaries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: being able to kind of trace it and figure out what happened is like if it's important in in in software engineering, it's 10x as important

takeaways.technique: Readable sequential workflow definitions over graph-node APIs
takeaways.what_they_do: Prefer fluent, top-to-bottom workflow code that teams can read and debug over node/edge graph APIs that require graph theory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I do not think you should need to learn graph theory to write workflows to build production applications.
